citation: Department of Microbiology, Government Medical College Srinagar. Antibiogram 2024 (January to December 2024). Srinagar: Government Medical College; 2025.
reporting: Percent susceptible. Overall tables for Gram-negative (Table 5) and Gram-positive (Table 6) priority pathogens from all specimens and locations, with the number of isolates; blood, urine and pus tables (Tables 7 to 12) by location (IPD, OPD, ICU) with the number of isolates per location. WHO priority pathogens only.
method: WHONET aggregate data; one result per patient per specimen type and pathogen (4533 reported isolates deduplicated to 3922 unique patient isolates). AST method and breakpoint standard not stated.

verification.note: Tables 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 10 and 11 parsed from the PDF text layer (cells assigned by the table ruling lines and word positions); Tables 6, 8 and 12 (incomplete ruling) entered from the text-layer word lines. Every value, n and location label was then compared by eye with the rendered page images (scale 2.5 whole pages; Tables 7, 9 and 11 again at scale 3.2 in two halves each), 2026-09-26.

notes: Antibiogram of WHO priority pathogens (Acinetobacter, Pseudomonas, E. coli, Klebsiella, Salmonella, S. aureus, Enterococcus) at GMC Srinagar, deduplicated with WHONET. IPD (inpatient wards) is recorded as ward; ICU is a separate column throughout. Overall Tables 5 and 6 (no specimen or location split) are recorded as all specimens, all settings. The "Number of isolates" printed in Tables 5 and 6 (e.g. E. coli 1045, S. aureus 878) is higher for every organism than the counts of Tables 1 and 3 (E. coli 976, S. aureus 775); both are recorded as printed. For E. coli, S. aureus and Enterococcus the Table 5 and 6 numbers match the unlabelled "By Isolate" (before deduplication) bars of Figure 3 (about 1045, 878 and 370), so the overall tables may count isolates before deduplication, although the report says the deduplicated file was used for AST; Figure 3 matches neither table for Klebsiella, Pseudomonas or Acinetobacter. Table 6 prints S. aureus co-trimoxazole 100.0, which the pus table (75% and 85%) contradicts (marked as a conflict). The source prints 0 in every drug column of strata with no isolates (e.g. blood OPD), so some printed zeros in small strata may stand for no result; they are kept as printed and zero-isolate rows are not extracted. Every printed 0 was checked by the second reader: a 0 for a drug that no table of this report shows tested for that organism, and a 0 that the January to June 2024 report of the same department contradicts (it prints a higher figure for isolates that are part of the full-year stratum, or "-" for the same isolates), is marked as a conflict; the other 0s are for drugs this report shows tested for the organism and may be real. Vancomycin for S. aureus is "Mic Nd" or "Not Done" everywhere except the urine table, which prints 0 (kept, marked as a conflict). Table 5 prints "-" (not tested) for Klebsiella ampicillin-sulbactam and Pseudomonas cefepime, but the blood, urine and pus tables print values for them (mostly 0); those cells are marked as conflicts. Counts: Table 1 (all specimens by location, 3924 isolates including 2 Salmonella), Table 3 (by specimen, all locations; the tracheal aspirate and respiratory sample columns are both recorded as respiratory, so each organism has two respiratory entries), and the strata Tables 7, 10 and 11 print with 0 isolates. Table 1 counts 6 ICU Enterococcus isolates while the blood, urine and pus tables list 3, 4 and 1 ICU isolates. The report states that percentages from more than 30 isolates are considered significant. Burkholderia (blood only) and Proteus mirabilis (pus only) appear in the specimen tables but not in Tables 1 and 3. The January to June 2024 report (GMC_SRINAGAR_2024_H1) also disagrees with some non-zero full-year figures by more than its isolates allow (e.g. blood IPD Burkholderia ceftazidime 73% here against 18.5% for 38 of the 48 isolates there); those figures are kept as printed.
issues: Second reader 2026-09-26: all 510 cells (seeded sample 128), all 60 row n, organisms and settings, and all 63 counts (Tables 1 and 3 and the zero strata) re-read against the page images (whole pages at scale 2.5, table crops at scale 3 to 4) before comparing with the file; 0 transcription errors and no IPD/OPD/ICU swaps (Table 8 lists Enterococcus as IPD, ICU, OPD and S. aureus as IPD, OPD, ICU; both mapped correctly).

Cells not kept confirmed as printed: 10 intrinsic (Table 5 Pseudomonas co-trimoxazole 100; blood Burkholderia amikacin and gentamicin; urine Pseudomonas ceftriaxone 0; pus Proteus tetracycline 0) and 6 percentages no whole number of isolates gives (urine ICU E. coli fosfomycin 92, urine ICU Klebsiella fosfomycin 70, urine OPD Acinetobacter ampicillin-sulbactam 70, pus ICU E. coli imipenem and meropenem 60, urine IPD S. aureus fosfomycin 98).

The 13 Table 5 conflicts are confirmed: Table 5 prints "-" for Klebsiella ampicillin-sulbactam (the blood, urine and pus tables print 0 in all 8 strata with isolates) and for Pseudomonas cefepime (blood IPD 0 and ICU 0, urine IPD 50, OPD 83, ICU 0; the pus table prints "-"). The 2 S. aureus urine vancomycin 0 conflicts are also confirmed (Mic Nd or Not Done in Tables 6, 8 and 12).

Zeros: the file has 132 printed 0s. 32 are for a drug that no table of this report shows tested for that organism (Table 5 or 6 prints "-", blank, IR or Mic Nd, or the organism is not in Table 5 and every one of its rows prints 0); 10 already had a conflict (8 Klebsiella ampicillin-sulbactam, 2 S. aureus vancomycin) and 22 got one: blood ICU E. coli tetracycline; blood IPD and ICU Burkholderia ciprofloxacin, imipenem, meropenem, piperacillin-tazobactam and tetracycline, and ICU amoxicillin-clavulanate; urine Pseudomonas ceftriaxone and fosfomycin (IPD, OPD, ICU); pus IPD and OPD Proteus ampicillin-sulbactam and tetracycline.

26 more 0s are for drugs this report shows tested, but the January to June 2024 report (same department, its isolates part of the full-year strata) contradicts them; 3 already had a conflict (Pseudomonas cefepime) and 23 got one naming the January to June figure: it prints a figure above 0 for blood ICU E. coli cefepime (100%, n=4), blood ICU P. aeruginosa gentamicin, aztreonam, ciprofloxacin, imipenem, meropenem and piperacillin-tazobactam (n=20 of 25), blood ICU B. cepacia ceftazidime (41.7%, same 28 isolates), urine ICU E. coli imipenem and meropenem (75%, n=4), urine OPD K. pneumoniae amikacin (53.3%, n=15), urine ICU P. aeruginosa imipenem (100%, n=1), blood OPD Enterococcus ampicillin and vancomycin (100%, same single isolate) and urine ICU Enterococcus ampicillin (33.3%, n=3); or it prints "-" (not tested) for the same isolates: blood ICU Klebsiella amikacin, gentamicin, ciprofloxacin, meropenem, piperacillin-tazobactam and tetracycline (1 isolate), blood ICU Burkholderia gentamicin (28), blood OPD Enterococcus erythromycin (1).

The other 74 zeros are for drugs this report shows tested for the organism and are kept without a conflict; the January to June 2024 report also prints 0, prints no result, or has no matching stratum (pus). Doubtful but without evidence either way: urine OPD Pseudomonas ciprofloxacin 0 (n=29, IPD 41), urine OPD S. aureus teicoplanin 0 (n=11, IPD 77), pus OPD Klebsiella amoxicillin-clavulanate, cefepime and imipenem 0 (n=25, with ceftriaxone 9 and meropenem 23), and the other single-isolate rows (the blood ICU Klebsiella isolate shows this report printing 0 for drugs that were not tested).
Added a conflict to overall S. aureus co-trimoxazole 100.0 (Table 6): the pus table prints 75% (IPD, n=503) and 85% (OPD, n=128).

Overall isolate numbers: the Table 5 and 6 row notes are correct (E. coli 1045, Klebsiella 904, Pseudomonas 604, Acinetobacter 525, Enterococcus 370, S. aureus 878 against 976, 811, 532, 482, 346 and 775 in Tables 1 and 3, and the Table 6 location splits 283/78/9 and 706/157/15 against 262/78/6 and 610/141/24). Figure 3 (no data labels) measures about 1045 E. coli, 878 S. aureus and 370 Enterococcus isolates before deduplication, so Tables 5 and 6 may be built from the isolates before deduplication; added to notes.

Not changed, for the lead: non-zero figures that the January to June 2024 report makes impossible if its isolates are part of the full-year strata: blood IPD Burkholderia ceftazidime 73 (18.5%, n=38; at most about 40% possible; row note added), urine ICU E. coli piperacillin-tazobactam 100 (50%, n=4), blood IPD Enterococcus ampicillin 10 (55%, n=30), urine IPD Klebsiella meropenem 70 (K. pneumoniae 9.7%, n=41), urine OPD S. aureus cefoxitin 88 (33.3%, n=3), blood IPD Enterococcus and S. aureus linezolid 100 (93.3% and 96.7%). Blood OPD Acinetobacter has 0 isolates here but 2 in the January to June report.

Lead 2026-09-26: 25 figures cannot be reconciled with the January to June 2024 report (its isolates are part of this full-year report; the implied July to December share would fall outside 0 to 100%): marked as source conflicts.
